text:
alex (ceo): thanks everyone for joining today. quick follow-up to the Q&A thread: folks asked for a concise narrative we can all use when talking to customers. the high-level: Mission unchanged — make inference predictable, economical, and portable. positioning: weplay both developer-first and production-first. that means we move fast for PLG but ship the reliability and controls enterprises need.

jess (marketing): can you give a one-sentence elevator pitch we can use in email headers and slides? something thatsizzes but isnt too buzzwordy.

alex (ceo): try: "Redwood: a production-first inference platform that delivers predictable latency, lower unit costs, and a single API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments." send suggestions and marketing will refine.

lee (cto): from an engineering perspective, whats should we emphasize to customers who ask about "how"? wed get fewer technical back-and-forths if sales mention the right signals.

alex (ceo): good Q. short technical callouts: high-throughput runtime, workload-aware batching & KV prefix caching, and smart routing that falls back across compatible model families for reliability. avoid deep internals in outbound copy but include a technical appendix for SRE/SEs.

rachel (pm): product question: roadmap conflict — do we recon on prioritizing latency SLO improvements vs richer rollout controls? both have sales asks.

lee (cto): suggested trade: push a small latency SLO sprint (profiling + default quantization profiles) to unblock top 3 Dedicated deals, while keeping the rollout controls backlog on a 2-sprint cadence.

alex (ceo): approved. engineering: make the Dedicated deal list visible to product so we can make data-driven tradeoffs. ops: please capture any required infra spend.

tom (ops): noted. will compile infra impacts and estimated cost delta for the sprint.

ops-bot: created ticket T-4902 in #product-ops: "Publish one-line pitch + technical appendix + updated roadmap prioritization" assigned to @jess and @rachel, due in 4 business days.

alex (ceo): thanks. final ask: when talking to customers about competitors, use contrast lines rather than direct name-calls. e.g., "Unlike some offerings focused only on model access or only on on-prem, Redwood unifies developer velocity with predictable production economics." keep it concise.

jess (marketing): will draft two headline variants (plain + technical) and post in #marketing for review.

alex (ceo): great. i'll follow up with a 1-pager and the list of priority deals for engineering. if anyone has strong objections to the trade decisions, DM me or drop notes in the product-roadmap thread. :thumbsup:
